desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list with n nodes is given by two arrays. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1; node 0 is the head, vals[i] is the value stored in node i and succ[i] is the number of the node after node i, or -1 if there is none. The node numbers say nothing about the order in the list: follow succ to find it.

All values in the list are distinct, and the list has no cycle. The array marked holds some values (they may even include values that do not occur in the list). A component is a maximal group of nodes that are next to each other in the list and whose values are all in marked. Return the number of components.

Example: vals = [10,20,30,40], succ = [1,2,3,-1] is the list 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40. With marked = [10,20,40] the groups are 10 -> 20 and 40, so the answer is 2.
constraints: The list starting at node 0 visits all n nodes and ends at a node with succ = -1
hints: Convert marked into a set so that you can test a value in O(1).
A component starts at a node that is marked while the node just before it is not marked (or it is the head).
Walk the list once keeping a flag prevMarked. Whenever the current node is marked and prevMarked is false, a new component begins: add one.
editorial: Counting components is the same as counting their first nodes. A node is the first node of a component exactly when it is marked and its predecessor is missing or unmarked. So walk the list once, remember whether the previous node was marked, and add one at every false-to-true change.
The marked values go into a hash set, so each membership test is O(1) and the whole pass takes O(n + m) time with O(m) extra space for the set.
solution:
def countComponents(vals, succ, marked):
    inside = set(marked)
    count = 0
    prev_marked = False
    cur = 0
    while cur != -1:
        now = vals[cur] in inside
        if now and not prev_marked:
            count += 1
        prev_marked = now
        cur = succ[cur]
    return count
